rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into geopolitics / policy_regulation / elections_public_opinion) are working keywords today. Day-of-year 310 sets ORDER only: group start index 310 % 3 = 1 (geopolitics leads, then policy_regulation, then elections_public_opinion; yesterday elections led), and within each group the list starts at offset 310 % group_size in pool order (geopolitics 10 -> 0: chip export controls first; policy 15 -> 10: state AI law first; elections 9 -> 4: content provenance C2PA first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-05, so items published 11-05 (after the prior harvest) through 11-06 are in scope. Context: Friday, three days after the US midterm Election Day; lame-duck Congress returns mid-November; informal European Council in Dublin on AI is 2026-11-13 (official pre-meeting papers/draft declarations are new, previews are not); Meta's new commercial terms on AI scraping take effect 2026-11-20 (courts in Norway and Brazil already suspended them). In scope: official post-election statements/after-action reports on AI-enabled interference (CISA/FBI/ODNI, state election officials), platform post-election takedown/labeling reports, certified (not early-return) results of AI-specific ballot measures only if they change the 11-05 picture, FEC/FCC actions, bills introduced/marked up, agency rules, court rulings, export-control actions. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, 'AI was the big issue of the midterms' commentary. Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
